title: Entrusted (Kern ch. 27)
hook: the Buddha entrusts the teaching to the bodhisattvas; the Lotus closed

segments.voice: Yesterday, Samantabhadra promised to come on a white elephant to anyone who keeps the sutra. Your line: kept and protected. Did you keep your one small practice? Day one thousand one hundred eighty-four.

A set of keys passes from one hand to another. A night nurse walks the morning shift through each patient's chart. A shop changes hands, and the old owner stands in the doorway one last time. Handing something over is its own small ceremony. The Lotus Sutra ends with one. In the last chapter of Kern's ordering, the Buddha rises from his seat, turns to the great crowd of bodhisattvas, and gives them the teaching to carry. Today: entrusted.
screen: `KEYS, A CHART, A SHOP.` → `HANDING OVER IS A CEREMONY.` → `THE LOTUS ENDS WITH ONE.`

segments.voice: Here's the scene, paraphrased. The Buddha stands, and by his power he reaches out his right hand to the bodhisattvas. Then he speaks, roughly like this. Over ages beyond counting I worked to reach this supreme awakening. Now I hand it to you. Take it, keep it, and make it known widely, so that all beings may hear it. The bodhisattvas bow, filled with joy, and answer together: we will do as the Lord commands. Do not be concerned. And they say it again. Then the Buddha sends home the Buddhas who had gathered from other worlds to hear him, and the assembly rejoices. That's how the Lotus closes, in Kern's order. Not with a final parable. With a handoff. The teaching doesn't stay with the teacher. It moves into other hands. Look back at the whole Lotus now. A ray of light from the Buddha's brow. Skillful means and one vehicle. A burning house, a lost son, rain falling on every plant. A phantom city to rest in, and a jewel sewn in a coat. A stupa in the sky, and the dragon king's daughter. Bodhisattvas rising from the cracks of the earth, and a Buddha whose life is long beyond counting. Never Disparaging, bowing to everyone. Guanyin hearing cries. Two sons leading a king, and Samantabhadra's promise. And at the end, a hand held out to the listeners: this is yours now.
screen: `THE BUDDHA RISES FROM HIS SEAT.` · `TAKE IT, KEEP IT, MAKE IT KNOWN.` · `WE WILL DO AS THE LORD COMMANDS.` · `THE WHOLE LOTUS, LOOKED BACK ON.` · then, large: `ENTRUSTED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: entrust something to someone. Settle, and let the breath slow. Think of one thing you've been holding alone. A task. A story about your family that only you remember. A way of making something. A small responsibility you keep doing because no one else knows how. Now bring to mind someone who could hold it. Picture handing it to them, and picture your hands empty afterward. Notice whether you want to take it back. You don't have to decide anything now. Just let the handoff happen in your mind once. The bell holds the time.
Entrusted. The Lotus closes with the Buddha handing the teaching to the bodhisattvas: take it, keep it, make it known. Today's word.

Your line: entrusted. Today, hand one real thing over, a job, a skill, a story, and don't hover while they do it. That closes the Lotus. Tomorrow we step back and look at the rest of the shelf. Day one thousand one hundred eighty-four.

howItsDone: Communities that keep the Lotus Sutra read its entrustment as the Buddha handing the teaching to the bodhisattvas, and some readers treat reciting, copying or teaching the sutra as a way of taking up that charge.

original.note: Sanskrit: the title of the Lotus Sutra, the lotus of the true dharma. today it closes.

what it means: the Buddha hands the teaching to the bodhisattvas and asks them to keep it and spread it.
what a scholar hears: in Kern's order the sutra closes not on a parable but on a handoff, the teaching passing from the teacher into many hands.

notes: Entrustment paraphrased from Kern (1884) ch. 27, not quoted. Confirm: the Buddha rises, by his power takes the bodhisattvas by the right hand / lays his right hand on them (Kumarajiva: strokes their heads three times; left out), the charge to keep and spread, the bodhisattvas' joint answer repeated, the visiting Buddhas dismissed.
'Over ages beyond counting I worked to reach this awakening' is a paraphrase; confirm the sense.

Placement claim: in Kumarajiva's Chinese (T 262) the entrustment is ch. 22, directly after the chapter on the Tathagata's supernatural power; in the Sanskrit and Kern it is last. Confirm, and confirm 'chanted across much of East Asia' for Kumarajiva's version.
Block look-back names days 1150–1183 by their index titles; confirm it matches the scripts as written.
howItsDone: 'many East Asian Buddhists recite, copy or teach it' is a general reception claim; soften or confirm.
